events.title: Intel Founded
events.desc: Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore rename the newly formed company NM Electronics to Intel Corporation, laying the foundation for decades of technological innovation.

events.title: First Microprocessor
events.desc: Intel debuts the 4004, the world's first commercial microprocessor, igniting the microprocessor revolution and propelling the future of computing devices.

events.title: 8086 Processor
events.desc: Launch of the 8086 processor, establishing the x86 architecture that drives countless PCs and servers in the modern era.

events.title: 386 Processor
events.desc: Intel introduces the 386 processor with 32-bit architecture, ushering in a new era of performance and multitasking for personal computers.

events.title: Peak GHG Emissions
events.desc: This year marks Intel's highest annual greenhouse gas emissions for operations. Over subsequent years, Intel invests heavily in chemical abatement, renewable energy, and energy-efficient manufacturing to reverse this trend.

events.title: RISE Strategy
events.desc: Intel launches its RISE (Responsible, Inclusive, Sustainable, Enabling) strategy and 2030 goals, aiming to drive industry-wide progress on climate action, water stewardship, and waste reduction.

events.title: Net-Zero By 2040
events.desc: Intel announces its commitment to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions (Scope 1 and 2) across its global operations by 2040, building on years of environmental initiatives.

events.title: Renewable Electricity
events.desc: The company achieves 99% renewable electricity usage worldwide, helping to drastically lower carbon emissions and driving progress toward Intel's long-term sustainability goals.

events.title: Sustainability Summit
events.desc: Intel hosts its first Sustainability Summit, uniting suppliers, government officials, and industry leaders to collaborate on next-generation sustainable semiconductor manufacturing.
